channel.title: VJs TV
channel.description: The global broadcast network for VJ culture. Live performances, artist discovery, and the technology powering visual art worldwide.

item.title: Fête des Lumières Lyon 2026 — Lyon, France
item.description: Fête des Lumières Lyon 2026 — one of the world's oldest and most prestigious light festivals with over 2 million visitors across four nights.

item.title: GLOW Eindhoven 2026 — Eindhoven, Netherlands
item.description: GLOW Eindhoven 2026 — a massive light art event hosting VJ teams for building-sized projection mapping projects across the city.

item.title: Signal Festival Prague 2026 — Prague, Czech Republic
item.description: Signal Festival Prague — a major festival featuring high-tech light installations and VJ performances across Prague's historic architecture.

item.title: Aavistus Festival 2026 — Helsinki, Finland
item.description: Aavistus 2026 — Biennial of Audiovisual Art & VJ Culture. Theme: 'Attention, please!' Open call for VJ sets, media art, and experimental works.

item.title: Ars Electronica 2026 — Linz, Austria
item.description: Ars Electronica Linz — the world's leading media art festival with large-scale immersive visuals, DEEP SPACE 8K projections, and the Prix Ars Electronica awards.

item.title: Burning Man 2026 — Black Rock Desert, Nevada, USA
item.description: Burning Man 2026 — the world's most experimental art event. VJs and visual artists create large-scale immersive projections and interactive installations on the playa.

item.title: MUTEK Montréal 2026 — Edition 27 — Quartier des spectacles, Montréal, Canada
item.description: MUTEK Montréal 2026 (Edition 27) — heavy focus on live VJ/AV integration. First wave: Jeff Mills, Rival Consoles, Ben UFO, Voices From The Lake, Polygonia.

item.title: Mo:Dem Festival 2026 — France (venue TBA)
item.description: Mo:Dem 2026 — a multi-day immersive AV camp where VJs treat visuals as the face, heartbeat, and dimension of the underground experience.

item.title: Tomorrowland Belgium 2026 — Boom, Belgium
item.description: Tomorrowland 2026 — the world's most iconic electronic music festival with elaborate stage designs, LED spectacles, and VJ content across all stages.

item.title: Sónar Barcelona 2026 — Fira Gran Via, Barcelona, Spain
item.description: Sónar Barcelona 2026 — one of the world's premier platforms for VJs and AV artists at Fira Gran Via. June 18–20.

item.title: Primavera Sound Barcelona 2026 — Parc del Fòrum, Barcelona, Spain
item.description: Primavera Sound 2026 — Barcelona's celebrated music festival with significant VJ and visual artist opportunities across multiple stages.

item.title: TOKYO LIGHTS 2026 — 1 Minute Projection Mapping Competition — Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building, Japan
item.description: One of the world's biggest projection mapping competitions — international artists map the iconic Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building with 1-minute loops.

item.title: EDC Las Vegas 2026 — Las Vegas Motor Speedway, Nevada, USA
item.description: Electric Daisy Carnival Las Vegas — one of the world's largest EDM festivals with massive LED stage visuals and VJ opportunities across multiple stages.

item.title: Mapping Festival 2026 — Geneva, Switzerland
item.description: Mapping Festival Geneva — no fixed theme, open call for real-time AV systems, hybrid art–science works, and club-scale VJ performances.

item.title: VJs TV Live Session 003 — Online / Amsterdam
item.description: The third VJs TV live stream: fractal generative art meets AI visuals in a one-hour live broadcast from Amsterdam.

item.title: Video Mapping Festival 2026 — Lille + Hauts-de-France, France
item.description: 9th edition — international artist residencies, building façade mapping, and professional/student projection mapping contests across the Hauts-de-France region.

item.title: Sónar Istanbul 2026 — Istanbul, Turkey
item.description: Sónar Istanbul — a hub for advanced music and technology with high-end visual production where electronic music meets cutting-edge AV performance.

item.title: Coachella Valley Music & Arts Festival 2026 — Indio, California, USA
item.description: Coachella 2026 — one of the world's largest festivals demanding continuous high-end VJ and visual content across multiple stages and installations.

item.title: Athens Digital Arts Festival (ADAF) 2026 — Athens, Greece
item.description: ADAF focuses on digital innovation and immersive audiovisual works. One of Southern Europe's leading platforms for digital art and VJ culture.

item.title: MUTEK Visuals Showcase — Montreal, Canada
item.description: A curated showcase of visual performances at MUTEK Festival, featuring projection mapping and AI-driven visuals.

item.title: Flux @ MUTEK Montreal 2025 — Montreal, Canada
item.description: Two of the world's leading VJ collectives perform simultaneously at MUTEK's main stage in a landmark cross-continental collaboration.

item.title: VJs TV Live Session 001 — Online / Berlin
item.description: The inaugural VJs TV live stream session featuring two of the most exciting visual artists working today.

item.title: Glitch Cathedral World Premiere — London, UK
item.description: The world premiere of Pixel Storm's Glitch Cathedral projection mapping onto a 400-year-old cathedral facade in East London.

item.title: Beeple — South Carolina, USA
item.description: Mike Winkelmann — known globally as Beeple — is the digital artist behind the Everydays project, a 5,000-consecutive-day streak of daily renders that became one of the defining works in digital art history. His work spans motion graphics for live concerts, dystopian CGI environments, and NFT milestones that reshaped the conversation around digital ownership.

item.title: Joanie Lemercier — Brussels, Belgium
item.description: Belgium-based visual artist whose projection installations create geometric light sculptures from minimal hardware. Lemercier's work induces genuine perceptual shifts — using a single projector to generate the illusion of three-dimensional forms floating in space, drawing on precise optics rather than computational complexity.

item.title: Memo Akten — Los Angeles, USA
item.description: Turkish-born multidisciplinary artist based in Los Angeles whose practice spans machine learning, interactive installation, and live performance. Memo Akten's work investigates the nature of consciousness, perception, and creativity through computational systems — creating artworks that use neural networks as a medium for philosophical inquiry.

item.title: Pablo Valbuena — Madrid, Spain
item.description: Madrid-based artist working with time, light, and space to create site-specific interventions that augment the perception of architecture. Pablo Valbuena's 'Augmented Sculpture Series' and light installations dissolve the boundary between physical structure and projected image — revealing hidden spatial dimensions with minimal means.

item.title: Quayola — Roma, Italy
item.description: Roma-based Italian artist working at the intersection of computational art, classical culture, and live audiovisual performance. Quayola translates art history, music, and nature into hybrid digital experiences of extraordinary precision and beauty.

item.title: Refik Anadol — Los Angeles, CA, USA
item.description: Turkish-American artist and director working with artificial intelligence and machine learning to create monumental immersive installations and live performances. Refik Anadol's work explores the intersection of art, technology, and human consciousness — transforming data into visual poetry at unprecedented scale.

item.title: Romain Tardy — Paris, France
item.description: French visual artist and co-founder of AntiVJ — the collective that defined a generation of projection art. Romain Tardy creates large-scale projection installations that treat light as a primary material — geometric, minimal, and architecturally precise works that have been exhibited at major institutions worldwide.

item.title: Ryoichi Kurokawa — Japan / International
item.description: Japanese audiovisual artist whose installations translate physical and mathematical phenomena into precise, meditative sensory experiences. His work operates at the intersection of sound, light, and scientific inquiry.

item.title: Ryoji Ikeda — Paris, France
item.description: Japanese electronic musician and visual artist based in Paris — the undisputed master of data aesthetics. Ikeda's work transforms raw data — binary code, mathematical sequences, scientific datasets — into audiovisual experiences of extreme precision and overwhelming sensory intensity. His 'test pattern' series and 'data.tron' are among the most important artworks of the 21st century.

item.title: Sougwen Chung — London, UK
item.description: London-based artist and researcher whose practice explores the intersection of hand-drawn mark-making and machine learning, creating large-scale installations and performances where human and algorithmic creativity become indistinguishable.

item.title: Yannick Jacquet — Brussels, Belgium
item.description: Belgian visual artist and co-founder of AntiVJ — one of the world's most influential collectives in projection art. Yannick Jacquet creates minimal, architecturally precise projection works that use light as a sculptural material, transforming physical surfaces into geometrically activated fields.

item.title: Denial of Service — Berlin, Germany
item.description: Berlin-based visual studio creating motion graphics, visual identities, and moving image work for cultural clients, music artists, and events. denial of service brings a strong graphic design sensibility to moving image — creating work that is typographically precise and formally intelligent.

item.title: DocOptic — USA
item.description: DocOptic is a working VJ, audiovisual artist, and training provider focused on live visuals performance. Their practice bridges the gap between technical craft and stage-ready output — producing loop content, live AV mixes, and educational material that has helped build the next generation of VJ practitioners.

item.title: Hexeosis — International
item.description: Hexeosis is a digital art project active since 2013, producing geometric loops and abstract visual systems with a distinctive mathematical precision. Their work lives at the intersection of screen saver culture, generative art, and VJ-ready loop content — tightly crafted, infinitely repeatable, and unmistakably their own.

item.title: Jago VJ — Madrid, Spain
item.description: Madrid-based VJ and visual artist creating real-time abstract visual environments for electronic music performance. Jago VJ is one of Spain's most active and respected live visual practitioners — performing at major festivals and clubs across Europe with a technically precise and musically intelligent performance practice.

item.title: Néstor Lizalde — Zaragoza, España
item.description: Spanish-born Zaragoza-based artist and researcher working with machine learning, computer vision, and neural networks to create artworks that investigate how computational systems see and represent the world. Néstor Lizalde's practice combines technical research rigour with a strong visual intelligence.

item.title: Ratsi — Paris, France
item.description: Paris-based VJ and generative visual artist known for precisely structured abstract systems that evolve slowly across long sets. Ratsi's work lives at the intersection of mathematics and music — building visual environments from geometric primitives that respond to electronic music with rigorous intelligence.

item.title: Robert Seidel — Berlin, Germany
item.description: Berlin-based artist working at the intersection of generative imagery, projection sculpture, and expanded cinema. Seidel creates works that dissolve the boundary between screen and space, image and object.

item.title: Synaesthesik — Amsterdam, Netherlands
item.description: Amsterdam-based powerhouse known for creating ultra-synced stage designs where light and video are so tightly locked to the kick drum they feel like a single instrument. Specialists in Visual Music — the philosophy that sound and image are one.

item.title: Thomas Vaquié — Paris, France
item.description: Paris-based VJ and visual artist creating audiovisual performances at the intersection of electronic music and abstract image-making. Thomas Vaquié builds live visual performances with the structural discipline of music composition — creating systems that evolve across a set with narrative intelligence.

item.title: Seeper Wrapped 2024 by seeper (2024)
item.description: seeper Wrapped 2024 — a documentation of the studio's most recent commissions, installations, and interactive experiences across a year of work. A snapshot of one of London's most consistently innovative art and technology studios at the frontier of interactive and immersive experience design.

item.title: Little Big City Beijing by seeper (2023)
item.description: Little Big City Beijing — seeper's immersive installation for a major Beijing attraction, creating a miniature city environment enhanced by projection mapping and interactive technology. A large-scale experiential design work demonstrating seeper's international reach and capability for complex immersive environments.

item.title: Re-Assembli by Ryoichi Kurokawa (2022)
item.description: re-assembli by Ryoichi Kurokawa — Installation, 2022. 2ch video | 4.1ch sound | 16ch strobe light. Duration: 8'00" loop. Building on the subassemblies series, this work uses laser-scanned 3D data from architectural structures, ruins, and natural elements—reassembled, distorted, and superimposed into dynamic, fragmented modules. The result is a layered exploration of time, decay, order/disorder, and the boundaries between human-made and organic worlds. The heavy use of synchronized strobe lighting (16 channels) creates overwhelming visual pulses that enhance perceptual disruption and immersion in the installation space.

item.title: Adventure Golf by seeper (2021)
item.description: seeper Adventure Golf — an immersive interactive experience design commission transforming the classic mini-golf format into a technology-enhanced environment, where projection mapping, sensor systems, and generative visuals respond to player actions across the course.

item.title: Origami Light Sculptures by Joanie Lemercier (2020)
item.description: A tutorial by Joanie Lemercier on creating light sculptures with origami and projection mapping — a hands-on guide to making small-scale geometric light art at home, developed during the 2020 lockdown period.

item.title: In S.Asmbli by Ryoichi Kurokawa (2020)
item.description: in s.asmbli (2020) by Ryoichi Kurokawa — VR 360 video | stereo sound version (alternative rendering) of the s.asmbli / subassemblies project. Laser-scanned 3D data from architecture, ruins, and nature are distorted, superimposed, and reassembled into dynamic modules, creating layered timelines of order/disorder that explore the interplay between human constructs and natural forces. Installation versions use 360 dome projection with Ambisonics; this VR excerpt offers immersive perceptual overload through algorithmic reconstruction. Duration: 6'48" full. Part of Kurokawa's ongoing exploration of data, architecture, and perception in immersive media.

item.title: CONSTELLATIONS by Joanie Lemercier (2019)
item.description: CONSTELLATIONS — an audiovisual installation for public spaces by Joanie Lemercier. Music by Paul Jebanasam. A geometric light work designed for outdoor architectural contexts — transforming public facades into cosmic maps of stars and constellations.

item.title: Subassemblies by Ryoichi Kurokawa (2019)
item.description: subassemblies by Ryoichi Kurokawa — 2019 concert version. Concept, direction, composition, and visuals by Ryoichi Kurokawa. Presented as video projection | 4.1ch sound | strobe light. Part of the subassemblies series, which uses 3D-scanned data from architecture, ruins, and natural elements to create superimposed, distorted reconstructions—blurring boundaries between human-made and organic forms in dynamic, perceptual audiovisual layers. This live iteration emphasizes immersive synchronization, intense strobing, and spatial audio for overwhelming, site-specific performance impact. Filmed/recorded excerpts appear in festival contexts (e.g., L.E.V., MIND THE FILM).

item.title: VJ set for Nina Kraviz @ DOUR Festival 2019 [excerpts] by VJ Emiko (2019)
item.category: Live VJ Performance / Audiovisual Set Excerpts
item.description: Excerpts from VJ Emiko's live visuals for Nina Kraviz's set at DOUR Festival 2019. Audio by Nina Kraviz. Visuals feature dynamic, high-energy mappings and effects tailored to the electronic/techno performance. Additional credits: cast Brena Over and Maniek Kłoczko; costume designers BOLA and Aleksandra Białk. A strong example of professional festival VJing with integrated live video footage and synchronized generative/animated content.

item.title: Engram : Data Sculpture for Melting Memories by Refik Anadol (2018)
item.category: Data-Driven Audiovisual Installation / Machine Learning Sculpture
item.description: Engram : Data Sculpture for Melting Memories by Refik Anadol (2018). Part of the Melting Memories series, this work uses machine intelligence to collect and interpret brainwave (EEG) data from participants recalling personal memories, then translates it into expressive, fluid data sculptures and dynamic visualizations. EEG signals are processed via custom algorithms to generate evolving particle systems, light forms, and immersive projections that evoke the ephemeral nature of memory and emotion. A contemplative exploration of human consciousness through AI, data as artistic material, and large-scale audiovisual expression—often presented as interactive installations or performative sculptures.

item.title: Onryō by denial of service (2017)
item.description: Onryō — Official music video by denial.of.service, combining industrial cybernetic aesthetics, reaction–diffusion systems, and sound-driven generative visuals. Created using 3DS Max, VRay, FumeFX, Processing, Max/Jitter, Ready, After Effects, PFTrack, and audio software including Ableton Live and NI FM8/Kontakt. The piece integrates motion reference, optical flow, and processed sequences inspired by Susi Sie’s 'Soundscapes'. Featured on The Creators Project / VICE and STASH #122.

item.title: Learning to See by Memo Akten (2017)
item.description: Learning to See — a neural network trained to interpret any visual input through a specific conceptual lens, demonstrating both the extraordinary capability and fundamental strangeness of how machine systems construct meaning from visual data.

item.title: Contour & Shape by denial of service (2017)
item.description: Contour & Shape — Official music video by denial.of.service. All visuals and audio created by the artist, combining human-data captured via Kinect v1, generative glitch and datamosh techniques, and 3D rendering in 3DS Max with Krakatoa + VRay. Processing3.x, Brekel, After Effects, Trapcode Form, and Python/Ruby scripts were used for complex generative and glitch effects. Audio features Roland TR-808, SH-101, Oberheim DMX, NordLead IIX, AKAI S-950, Yamaha CS15, Doepfer A-100, and NI Kontakt/Reaktor/FM8.

item.title: Archive Dreaming by Refik Anadol (2017)
item.category: Data-Driven Interactive Installation / Machine Learning Visualization
item.description: Archive Dreaming by Refik Anadol (2017) — commissioned by SALT Research to reinterpret their vast archive of over 1.7 million documents (images, texts, maps from Ottoman era to contemporary Turkey). Machine learning algorithms search, sort, and reveal hidden relations and clusters within the collection, transforming them into dynamic, generative visualizations projected as an immersive 'data dream' environment. Visitors interact via interface to navigate connections in architecture, art, urbanism, and culture—creating fluid, evolving dream-like forms that blend memory, history, and AI perception. A landmark in data art, public archive reinterpretation, and immersive media, awarded SEGD Global Design Honor and Best in...

item.title: ORANGE — Show Hello! by Superbien (2016)
item.description: A large-scale architectural projection mapping created by Superbien for ORANGE Telecom's Show Hello! 2016 product launch event. A kinetic feast of light, geometry, and colour on a monumental scale.

item.title: 2016 in Review by seeper (2016)
item.description: A festive year-in-review from seeper — a glimpse into 2016 across the studio's commissions, installations, and interactive experiences. Documents a period of sustained creative output from one of London's most influential art and technology collectives.

item.title: Seeper Showreel 2015 by seeper (2015)
item.description: seeper showreel 2015 — a panoramic overview of the studio's work at the intersection of art and technology since their founding in 1998. Spanning interactive projection mapping, immersive experiences, motion capture installations, and public interactive systems, the reel demonstrates the full range of seeper's pioneering practice.

item.title: Virtual Depictions: San Francisco by Refik Anadol (2015)
item.category: Public Art Installation / Parametric Data Sculpture
item.description: Virtual Depictions: San Francisco by Refik Anadol — a public art project consisting of series of parametric data sculptures that narrate the invisible layers of San Francisco's urban fabric. Using architectural scans, public data archives, environmental metrics, and computational techniques, the work generates dynamic, cinematic visualizations projected on large-scale video walls in building lobbies. In collaboration with Kilroy Realty Corporation and SOM Architects, it turns corporate/public spaces into immersive data-driven experiences—exploring memory, architecture, and city identity through generative media art. Awarded SEGD Global Design Award; a pivotal early work in Anadol's data/media architecture oeuvre.

item.title: Infinity Room - [TIEE] by Refik Anadol (2015)
item.category: Immersive Audiovisual Installation / Temporary Immersive Environment
item.description: Infinity Room - [TIEE] by Refik Anadol — an immersive environment project as part of the artist's ongoing 'Temporary Immersive Environment Experiments' (TIEE) series. Utilizes multi-channel digital projections, reflective surfaces/mirrors, generative algorithms, and synchronized sound to create an illusion of infinite, expanding space within a finite room. Viewers experience hallucinatory depth, endless recursion, and perceptual overload—blurring boundaries between physical architecture and virtual infinity. A seminal work in data/media-driven immersive art, emphasizing site-specific transformation and sensory immersion.

item.title: FUJI (不死) by Joanie Lemercier (2014)
item.description: FUJI (不死) — a 14-minute audiovisual installation by Joanie Lemercier. Music by Paul Jebanasam. A geometric light work creating the illusion of a mountain floating in darkness — pure sculptural projection questioning the boundaries of physical and projected space.

item.title: Tearing Shadows by Robert Seidel (2013)
item.description: A projection sculpture by Berlin-based artist Robert Seidel in which fragments of projection, physical sculpture, and spatial sound perfoliate the gallery space. Exhibited at 401contemporary Berlin.

item.title: Live with MiraCalix by Quayola (2013)
item.description: A live audiovisual concert by Quayola and Natan Sinigaglia, performed with music by Mira Calix. Recorded excerpts showcase the duo's real-time synthesis of abstract visual computation and electronic sound.

item.title: Daydream by nonotak (2013)
item.description: Daydream — stroboscopic light fields and spatial audio create a near-hallucinatory environment that challenges every viewer's sense of physical reality.

item.title: Chiaroscuro by Sougwen Chung (2013)
item.description: An immersive installation combining hand-drawn imagery at scale, projection mapping, LEDs, and spatial sound to create a dynamic interplay of light and shadow — the oldest dialogue in visual art.

item.title: CANCELLED END OF TIME by JAGO VJ (2013)
item.description: JAGO VJ — CANCELLED END OF TIME is a live VJ performance exploring abstraction, time, and immersive audiovisual textures. This piece features generative patterns and real-time manipulation synced to music for a unique live experience.

item.title: BREEDLE (Official Video) by denial of service (2013)
item.description: BREEDLE — Official music video by Extrawelt, with all visuals created by denial.of.service. The project took four months of formula experimentation and over 1000 hours of combined rendering using open-source raytracers. The video explores cyber-ecology, abstract electronic music visualization, photoreal depth of field, and Mandelbrot-inspired fractals. Sibling video for the track 'THE INKLING' can be found at https://vimeo.com/76123151.

item.title: Ryoji Ikeda :: supercodex [live set] by Ryoji Ikeda (2013)
item.description: Ryoji Ikeda :: supercodex [live set] — recorded November 8, 2013 at WWW, Tokyo. A full-force live performance in the supercodex series, transforming computational/mathematical data into overwhelming, synchronized audiovisual streams: high-speed glitches, binary/code visualizations, particle flows, and razor-sharp electronic sound. Exemplifies Ikeda's signature approach to precision, perception overload, and the sublime through data as artistic material. Part of his broader datamatics/supercodex body of work exploring infinity and algorithmic aesthetics in live contexts.

item.title: Ryoji Ikeda :: data.path by Ryoji Ikeda (2013)
item.description: Ryoji Ikeda :: data.path (26 SEP 2013 – 5 JAN 2014, Espacio Fundación Telefónica, Madrid, ES). Part of the datamatics series, this installation transforms vast streams of raw data (mathematical, scientific, computational) into overwhelming visual and sonic experiences. Features high-resolution projections of binary patterns, glitches, code flows, particle systems, and ultra-precise synchronization—exploring perception, infinity, and the sublime in data. A key example of minimalist, data-centric immersive art that pushes technical and sensory boundaries.

item.title: Sydney Opera House by Urban Screen (2012)
item.description: Urban Screen's audiovisual staging of the Sydney Opera House — a poetic homage to the architecture and the constructional concept of Jørn Utzon. As Utzon described it: the shells are like clouds. Urban Screen's projection responds to this with a visual programme that honours the building's own internal spatial and structural logic across its iconic shell forms.

item.title: Sagrada Familia: Ode à la Vie by Moment Factory (2012)
item.description: The first-ever projection mapping on the Nativity façade of Antoni Gaudí's Sagrada Familia, created by Moment Factory for La Mercè Festival 2012. A collaboration between the cities of Barcelona and Montreal.

item.title: 59 Productions — London, UK / New York, USA
item.description: The kings of projection design for theatre and large-scale cultural events. 59 Productions bridge high-art storytelling and technical projection mapping, with landmark commissions including the Sydney Opera House sails and the Tower of London.

item.title: AntiVJ — Europe (Distributed)
item.description: Founded by artists including Joanie Lemercier and Yannick Jacquet, AntiVJ is the gold standard for minimalist geometric projection mapping. More a visual label than a studio, it operates as a collective of independent masters of light united by a shared aesthetic philosophy.

item.title: D-Fuse — London, United Kingdom
item.description: London-based audiovisual collective founded by Mike Faulkner. Pioneers of live cinema and VJ culture since the mid-1990s, D-Fuse have shaped the language of moving image performance across three decades.

item.title: Derivative — Toronto, Canada
item.description: Toronto-based software studio and creators of TouchDesigner — the real-time visual development platform that has become the standard tool for live AV performance, interactive installation, and projection mapping worldwide. Derivative's influence on the field is incalculable.

item.title: fuse* — Modena, Italy
item.description: Italian masters of data-driven audiovisual art. Their project Dökk uses a dancer's heartbeat and brainwave data processed in real-time to generate visuals...

item.title: Marshmallow Laser Feast — London, UK
item.description: UK pioneers of immersive installation combining VR, LiDAR scanning, spatial audio, and biological data to create experiences that let audiences see invisible forces — from oxygen molecules to ancient forests. Creators of the landmark 'We Live in an Ocean of Air'.

item.title: Moment Factory — Montréal, Canada
item.description: The undisputed heavyweight of large-scale multimedia experience production. With offices in Paris, Tokyo, LA, London, and NYC, Moment Factory creates stadium-scale visual worlds for the world's biggest artists and most iconic public spaces.

item.title: nonotak — Paris, France
item.description: Paris-based light and sound art studio creating extraordinary immersive installations that use stroboscopic lighting, mirror systems, and spatial audio to generate near-hallucinatory perceptual experiences. Exhibited at Ars Electronica, Nuit Blanche, and KIKK Festival.

item.title: Quayola — London, UK
item.description: London-based Italian artist creating digital paintings, live AV performances, and immersive installations that reinterpret classical art and music through algorithmic processes. One of the most consistently rigorous figures in contemporary digital art.

item.title: Refik Anadol Studio — Los Angeles, USA
item.description: A Machine Intelligence lab rather than a conventional studio. Refik Anadol Studio turns massive datasets — from NASA archives to MoMA's collection — into fluid, hallucinatory 'Data Paintings'. In 2026, their permanent home Dataland opens in Los Angeles with 20,000 sq ft of AI-driven exhibition space.

item.title: Rhizomatiks — Tokyo, Japan
item.description: Led by Daito Manabe, Rhizomatiks is arguably the world's most advanced tech-art laboratory. Specialising in the intersection of drones, robotics, motion capture, and real-time AI, their 2026 projects involve live performances driven by dancers' brainwaves (ELEVENPLAY).

item.title: Studio DRIFT — Amsterdam, Netherlands
item.description: Amsterdam studio focused on 'Coded Nature' — using biological algorithms and industrial engineering to create kinetic light works. Famous for Shylight (flowers controlled by winches) and massive drone performances like 'Wind of Change' (2026), where light-emitting drones form 3D sculptures in night sky.

item.title: teamLab — Tokyo, Japan
item.description: Tokyo-based interdisciplinary art collective creating immersive digital art installations that blur boundaries between artwork and viewer. With permanent museums in Tokyo, Singapore, Shanghai, and beyond, teamLab are the most visited digital art institution in the world.

item.title: United Visual Artists — London, UK
item.description: Founded in London in 2003, United Visual Artists (UVA) creates large-scale immersive installations, live performance visuals, and permanent public artworks that sit at the intersection of light, time, and human experience.

item.title: Universal Everything — Sheffield, UK
item.description: Sheffield-based digital art studio whose 'Future Self' series of animated walking figures has shaped the visual language of contemporary digital art. Collaborators with Kanye West, Nike, and Mercedes-Benz — exhibited at the Tate and galleries worldwide.

item.title: United Visual Artists — London, UK
item.description: London-based art and technology studio creating large-scale light installations, live AV environments, and public commissions. Collaborators with Massive Attack, Chemical Brothers, and U2 — and creators of the permanent 'Volume' installation at the V&A.

item.title: VeeMee Visuals — Tilburg, Nederland
item.description: Dutch collective regarded as the gold standard for high-end festival VJing — managing visual identity for top DJs with flawless 3D content and stadium-scale...

item.title: WHITEvoid / DARK MATTER — Berlin, Germany
item.description: Founded by Christopher Bauder, WHITEvoid operates DARK MATTER — a 1,000m² former factory in East Berlin housing the TRANSFORMATOR, a permanent kinetic light installation used to prototype SKALAR, VEKTOR, and other landmark works. The gold standard for kinetic light art.

item.title: 1024 Architecture — Paris, France
item.description: Paris-based studio creating interactive installations, live AV performances, and generative architectural projections. Founded by architects Pier Schneider and Francois Wunschel — bringing genuine spatial intelligence to digital art at Nuit Blanche, Scopitone, and major European electronic venues.

item.title: Bart Kresa Studio — Los Angeles, USA
item.description: LA-based projection design studio specialising in large-scale architectural projections and live event visuals. Bart Kresa's studio has created seminal works for the Burning Man festival, major architectural commissions in the US and internationally, and landmark live production visuals.

item.title: Adobe After Effects by Adobe
item.description: Industry-standard motion graphics and visual effects software. VJs use After Effects to create animated loops, effects, and visual content for live performance.

item.title: Akai APC40 by Akai Professional
item.description: Professional MIDI controller built for Ableton Live but widely adopted by VJs. Its clip launch grid and fader bank map perfectly to visual performance workflows.

item.title: ArKaos GrandVJ by ArKaos
item.description: Professional VJ software and media server for live events. Layer-based mixing, effects, DMX control, and pixel mapping for clubs, touring, and broadcast.

item.title: Blackmagic Design by Blackmagic Design
item.description: Professional video hardware manufacturer. DeckLink capture cards, ATEM switchers, and HyperDeck recorders are standard in VJ and live production setups.

item.title: Blender by Blender Foundation
item.description: Free, open-source 3D creation suite. VJs and motion designers use Blender for modelling, animation, rendering, and creating visual content for live performance.

item.title: Cinema 4D by Maxon
item.description: Professional 3D motion design software. The industry standard for motion graphics and visual content creation used in broadcast, film, and live event visuals.

item.title: Disguise by Disguise
item.description: Industry-leading media server and virtual production platform used in world tours, broadcast, and XR stages. Trusted by the biggest names in live entertainment.

item.title: HeavyM by HeavyM
